audit.why: Both layers and the packet agree: Jayce owns levels 2-3 while Acceleration Gate out-ranges a melee farmer, Cho'Gath takes over from 4 onward, and the item stages are flatly his. The content prose is unusually honest about this ('I lose this outright') and matches the chart. No change needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why for level 6 is champion-wide boilerplate ('six abilities against his four') and never names Feast, its range, or why resistances do not help.
audit.why: Feast is 175 range and true damage. _missing-interactions.json flags this pair for resistances-invalidated, and the content layer already says extra Armor and MR do nothing — the full layer contradicted that by leaving the generic line in.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten around the 175 range and the true damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is built on tracking and baiting Rupture — 'stay outside his Rupture range while you poke', 'never facecheck a Cho'Gath who has Rupture and Feast up' — but Rupture is a flat 6-second cooldown at every rank.
audit.why: A 6s cooldown is not something you bait or count; it is always available. The correct instruction is a range instruction (950), not a timing one. Feral Scream is 300 range and 11s at rank 1, and Feast is 175 range — all three numbers turn vague respect into positioning.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], dosFull and dontsFull rewritten around the real numbers and ranges.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content mid and late sections are written in the first person — 'This is where it slips away from me', 'I lose this outright, and I have to be honest about it', 'My whole game has to be over before this stage'. Every other section of this same entry, including early and all seven whys, uses second person.
audit.why: The entry switches voice halfway through, which reads as a different author and breaks the coaching register the rest of the page holds.
audit.corrected: mid and late converted to second person within the length band.

edits.before: This is where it slips away from me. By 4-5 his Rupture knockup into Feral Scream silence punishes any step-up — the silence doesn't stop my R stance-swap (form-swapping works through silence), but it does lock out the cannon Q and Hyper Charge that carry my burst, so my poke goes dark mid-combo. At 6 it gets worse: Feast is a point-blank true-damage execute that ignores the fact that I build zero MR on a cannon page, so standing in Rupture range now risks a flat death. My R isn't an ult spike — it's just the stance toggle I already had — while his level 6 is a hard kill button. Keep poking from max gate range, never sit inside Rupture, and stop pretending the hammer all-in is still a kill.

edits.before: I lose this outright, and I have to be honest about it. Once he has one HP component and a few Feast stacks, my cannon-Q chip and hammer Q-E burst can't move his bar, and his percent-HP true-damage Feast deletes my squishy cannon frame in a single cast — extra Armor and MR do nothing against true damage. Unlike a poke-favoured tank lane, there's no \"spend the lead and out-DPS him\" line here; he scales clean past me. My one remaining tool is Thundering Blow's max-HP magic damage, but that's a peel/disengage button, not a kill. My whole game has to be over before this stage: take plates and roam off my early edge, give the side lane to a teammate who can actually duel him, and never facecheck a Cho'Gath who has Rupture and Feast up.

notes: UNVERIFIED, left untouched: content.mid asserts that Feral Scream's silence 'doesn't stop my R stance-swap (form-swapping works through silence)'. Nothing in champ-data/_kits confirms or denies this — needsResearch is empty, which the brief says means unknown, not no. It is a load-bearing claim (it tells the player he still has an escape mid-silence), so I neither restated nor removed it and it needs confirming before it ships. Separately, a derived-flag misfire to be aware of: _missing-interactions.json says 'Cho'Gath can deny your mobility (To the Skies!/Shock Blast (Q)) with Rupture (Q)' and the kit carries a grounding flag on Rupture, but Riot's own description of Rupture is only 'popping enemy units into the air, dealing damage and slowing them' — no grounding. Per the brief's instruction to trust the description over the flag, I wrote nothing about Rupture grounding your dash. The knockup interrupting you is real and already on the page.
